items.title: Cut Claude Code Bill by Routing to DeepSeek or Grok
items.why_it_matters: A new MCP router called Leanroute lets you cut Claude Code costs by up to 60% by automatically routing simpler tasks to cheaper models like DeepSeek. Since you use Claude Code daily and want to manage your API spend, this directly optimizes your workflow without sacrificing output quality. You can install this MCP server in your Claude Code configuration this week to start saving on your AI-ingest development costs.

items.title: A local bridge for bidirectional collaboration between Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: Agent-bridge is a new local tool that enables bidirectional collaboration between Claude Code and Codex, allowing them to work together on the same codebase. Since these are your two primary coding tools, this bridge lets you combine Codex's editor integration with Claude Code's terminal execution power. You can clone this repository and run it locally this week to let both tools collaborate on your AI-ingest project.

items.title: Muraqib, free nightly QA that lets Claude open a fix PR when tests fail
items.why_it_matters: Muraqib is an open-source tool that runs nightly QA tests on your repository and allows Claude to automatically open a pull request to fix any failures. As you build up your Git and commit discipline on AI-ingest, this automates the tedious debugging loop while keeping you in the director's chair. You can set up Muraqib on your GitHub repository this week to let Claude draft fixes for your Next.js build errors overnight.

items.title: Show HN: Seedeep – I couldn't see what Claude Code was doing, so I drew it
items.why_it_matters: Seedeep is a new open-source tool designed to visualize exactly what Claude Code is doing in your terminal in real-time. Since your goal is to get better at directing AI and verifying its work, having a visual map of its edits makes it much easier to spot mistakes before committing. You can run Seedeep alongside your next Claude Code session this week to visually audit its changes to your Next.js files.

items.title: OpenContext – Persistent, project-local memory for AI coding agents via MCP
items.why_it_matters: OpenContext is an MCP server that provides persistent, project-local memory for AI coding agents. This helps Claude Code remember your specific project structure, APIs, and decisions across different sessions instead of starting fresh every time. You can add the OpenContext MCP to your Claude Code setup this week to give it a persistent understanding of your Supabase schema and Next.js routes.

items.title: Show HN: Memnest, local-first memory shared by pi, Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: Memnest is a local-first shared memory tool that lets Claude Code and Codex share context and memory seamlessly. Instead of manually copying and pasting context between your terminal agent and your editor, Memnest keeps them in sync locally. You can install Memnest on your machine this week to keep your active project context unified across both of your coding environments.

items.title: Claude permanently raising weekly limits by 25%
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has permanently increased weekly usage limits for Claude by 25%. For your daily workflow, this means fewer interruptions and more runway to build without hitting rate-limit walls. You can take advantage of this extra capacity this week to run longer, uninterrupted coding sessions with Claude Code on your AI-ingest project.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude for Mac desktop app now has built-in browser
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic added a built-in browser to the Claude for Mac desktop app, allowing the model to view and interact with web pages directly. This makes it easier to debug frontend layouts or show Claude live documentation without leaving the chat. You can open the Claude Mac app this week and use the new browser to let Claude inspect your local Next.js development server.

items.title: Show HN: Tokensift, an open-sourced token-efficiency linter for LLM prompts
items.why_it_matters: Tokensift is an open-source token-efficiency linter that analyzes your LLM prompts to find and remove redundant tokens. Since you are building an AI-ingest tool that processes news feeds, keeping your prompts lean will directly reduce your API bills. You can run your AI-ingest prompt templates through Tokensift this week to optimize your token usage before your next deploy.
